'''Michael Latrent Harris'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Latrent Harris () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/153010-michael-latrent-harris |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=March 30, 2025}}</ref> (born June 15, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player.

==College career==
Harris played [[college basketball]] for [[Rice University]] and finished his career as Rice's all-time leading scorer (2,014 points) and rebounder (1,111 boards).

==Professional career==
Harris played professionally for [[BC Kyiv]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball Super League|Ukrainian Super League]] during the 2005–06 season. In the 2006–07 NBA preseason, Harris was signed by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]],<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/HarrisMcCray_060921.html | title = Bucks Sign Harris and McCray | date = September 21, 2006 | work = [[NBA.com]] | access-date = July 15, 2007}}</ref> with whom he averaged 6.0 points per game and 2.4 rebounds per game in five preseason games<ref name=rocketssignharris>[http://www.nba.com/nba_news/rockets_mikeharris_080308.html Rockets Sign Mike Harris to 10-Day Contract.]</ref> before being cut from the team before the regular season started. Harris then spent the 2006–07 season with the [[Colorado 14ers]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]].<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070207.html | title = Bucks, D-League Building Productive Pipeline | date = February 7, 2007 | first = Truman | last = Reed | access-date = July 15, 2007 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080316004818/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070207.html | archive-date = March 16, 2008 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He averaged 11.8 points per game, 6.8 rebounds per game and 1.54 blocks per game in 48 games with the 14ers during the 2006–07 season.<ref name=rocketssignharris/>

Harris then signed a non-guaranteed deal with the [[Houston Rockets]] on July 13, 2008,<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.insidehoops.com/harris-rockets-071307.shtml | title = Rockets sign Mike Harris to non-guaranteed deal | publisher = InsideHoops.com NewsWire | date = July 13, 2008 | access-date = July 15, 2007 }}</ref> and after averaging 5.0 points per game and 6.0 rebounds per game in Houston's first two preseason games, he was by waived the club before the season started on October 22.<ref name=rocketssignharris/>

In the 2007–08 season, Harris played for the [[Dongguan Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA), averaging 28 minutes played per game, with 24.3 points per game and 11.6 rebounds per game in 25 games played.<ref name=rocketssignharris/> Following the end of the CBA season, Harris signed a 10-day [[NBA]] contract with the [[Houston Rockets]] on March 9, 2008, and after that he earned a contract from the club for the remainder of the season, with a team option for the next season. During the 2008–09 NBA preseason, Harris was released once again by the Rockets.

In the 2009–2010 season, Harris was signed by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the D-League. After averaging 25.3 points with the Vipers, he was signed by the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/6784655.html Rockets sign Harris after Wafer fails physical]. Retrieved on December 23, 2009.</ref> On January 6, 2010, Harris was waived by Houston. Later that season, Harris briefly played for the [[Washington Wizards]], before rejoining the Vipers.<ref name=vipers>{{Cite web |url=http://www.krgv.com/sports/story/BREAKING-SPORTS-NEWS-Vipers-reacquire-Mike-Harris/P4oe1_XOTkaFsGuOKaabsg.cspx |title=Vipers reacquire Mike Harris |access-date=March 25, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303191736/http://www.krgv.com/sports/story/BREAKING-SPORTS-NEWS-Vipers-reacquire-Mike-Harris/P4oe1_XOTkaFsGuOKaabsg.cspx |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 24, 2010, he signed with the Houston Rockets for another stint.<ref>[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/65545/20100324/rockets_sign_harris_of_rio_grande_valley/ Rockets Sign Harris Of Rio Grande Valley] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100327221039/http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/65545/20100324/rockets_sign_harris_of_rio_grande_valley |date=March 27, 2010 }}</ref> He was reassigned to the Vipers on April 13, 2010. Harris was also named the 09-10 [[NBA D-League MVP]] along winning the [[NBA D-League]] Championship in a 2-0 victory over the 66ers. He posted 26 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2009_10/ |title=Transactions: 2009–10 Season |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090911062309/http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2009_10/ |archive-date=September 11, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the summer of 2012, Harris signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-announce-2012-13-training-camp-roster Wolves Announce 2012–13 Training Camp Roster]</ref> However, he was waived before the start of the 2012–13 season.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11314 Timberwolves waive Mike Harris and Chris Johnson]</ref> Later that fall, he signed with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] in China.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.niubball.com/teams/ |title=Niubball.com – Teams |access-date=November 23, 2012 |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203154411/http://www.niubball.com/teams/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> At the end of the Chinese season, he joined the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] in Puerto Rico.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/101043/leones-de-ponce-replace-garret-siler-with-mike-harris.html Leones de Ponce replace Garret Siler with Mike Harris]</ref> During that season, Harris was chosen the Most Valuable Player of the league, averaging 20.4 ppg and 10.2 rpg.

On September 26, 2013, he signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/09/26/jazz-sign-harris-mcguire-machado.ap/ |title=Jazz round out roster with three camp invites |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203095824/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/09/26/jazz-sign-harris-mcguire-machado.ap/ |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 7, 2014, he was waived by the Jazz after 20 games, averaging 4.2 points per game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waives-forward-mike-harris Jazz Waives Forward Mike Harris]</ref> On January 22, 2014, he signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] in China for the rest of the [[2013–14 CBA season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/110665/zhejiang-waive-ivan-johnson-sign-mike-harris.html Zhejiang waive Ivan Johnson, sign Mike Harris]</ref> At the end of the Chinese season, he re-signed with the Leones de Ponce of Puerto Rico.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/114862/mike-harris-joining-leones-de-ponce.html Mike Harris joining Leones de Ponce]</ref> Harris led the Leones de Ponce to the championship that season, and carried off the Finals MVP award. Harris was widely acclaimed as the best player in the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] during this time.

In September 2014, he returned to China and signed with the [[Qingdao Eagles]] for the [[2014–15 CBA season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/134789/qingdao-double-star-on-fire-finalizing-deal-with-mike-harris.html Qingdao Double Star on fire, finalizing deal with Mike Harris]</ref> On April 10, 2015, he re-signed with Leones de Ponce.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/157937/mike-harris-signs-with-leones-de-ponce.html Mike Harris signs with Leones de Ponce]</ref>

In October 2015, he signed with [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] for the [[2015–16 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=四川新赛季外援已敲定 哈达迪+哈里斯+邓特蒙|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2015-10-02/doc-ifximrxn8164510.shtml|access-date=December 7, 2015|work=sports.sina.com.cn|date=October 2, 2015|language=zh}}</ref> Harris helped lead Sichuan to their first-ever CBA title the following March, and re-signed with the Blue Whales for the [[2016-17 CBA season]], but missed much of the campaign with an injury.

Harris returned to Puerto Rico for another stint with the Leones de Ponce in the summer of 2017. He then signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] in China for the [[2017-18 CBA season]].

Since his [[2017-18 CBA season]] and departure from the [[Fujian Sturgeons]], he has had multiple different stints in different leagues overseas.

He announced his retirement in 2022.
